subject.name: Earth and Space Science 3

domains.name: Origin and evolution of the universe

standards.text: observational evidence such as galaxy recession rates, cosmic microwave background radiation, and the large-scale distribution of matter provides scientific support for models explaining the origin and evolution of the universe;

stars have measurable properties and life cycles that can be studied through spectral analysis and classification, and that planetary motions follow predictable patterns governed by gravitational laws;
various observational techniques enable the detection of planets beyond the solar system and provide evidence that helps scientists evaluate the possibility of life in other planetary systems;
advances in space exploration technologies enhance our understanding of Earth and other planets; and

satellite technology and remote sensing enable scientists and government agencies to observe Earth systems, monitor environmental changes, and support disaster risk reduction and environmental management.
satellite observations and remote sensing technologies provide critical data used to monitor Earth's climate system and environmental changes;
climate change results from natural processes and human activities that alter the balance of energy in Earth's climate system;
international agreements and national policies guide efforts to mitigate climate change and support adaptation strategies; and
climate mitigation and adaptation strategies can strengthen community resilience and reduce the impacts of climate change.

The learners can analyze observational and satellite data to explain models of the universe, classify stars and planetary systems, and evaluate evidence related to the existence of exoplanets and extraterrestrial life. They can apply scientific reasoning and digital tools to interpret astronomical and Earth observation data and communicate how space science and remote sensing technologies contribute to environmental monitoring and disaster risk management in the Philippines.

The learners can analyze satellite and climate datasets to explain climate change trends and their impacts on the Philippines. They can apply scientific reasoning and data analysis to evaluate climate mitigation and adaptation strategies and communicate evidence-based recommendations for strengthening community climate resilience and sustainability.

competencies.text: evaluate competing cosmological models using observational evidence, including galaxy recession rates, the age of the universe, and the large-scale structure of matter;
use redshift data and cosmic microwave background evidence to evaluate the Big Bang model;
analyze the timeline from the Big Bang to the formation of the first stars and galaxies;
analyze stellar spectra to classify stars using the Hertzsprung-Russel diagram;
apply Kepler’s laws to explain planetary orbital characteristics and habitability zones;
conduct investigation on the exoplanet detection methods and their relevance to astrobiology;
evaluate evidence from exoplanet research (e.g., atmospheric composition, temperature, and distance from a star) to assess conditions for extraterrestrial life;
identify key space technologies for space exploration and Earth observation and their primary functions;

use satellite imagery (e.g. from PhilSA Space Data Dashboard, NASA Worldview or Copernicus Browser) to analyze land cover change, deforestation, or urban expansion in a Philippine locality over time; and
evaluate how PhilSA and international space agencies use remote sensing data to monitor Philippine environment conditions and support disaster response.
use satellite-derived datasets including temperature anomalies, sea level measurements, and atmospheric CO₂ to identify climate trends in the Philippines;
use satellite and ocean observation data to analyze the sea level rise and its potential impacts on Philippine coastal communities;
explain how enhanced greenhouse effect and human activities contribute to global warming and climate change;
calculate personal or school-level carbon footprints and relate the results to national greenhouse gas emissions data;
describe the commitments of the Philippines under the Paris Agreement and their role in reducing greenhouse gas emissions;
analyze the provisions of Republic Act No. 9729 and explain how local government units implement climate adaptation plans;
describe the mitigation and adaptation strategies used in Philippine communities; and
create a community-level climate resilience plan integrating renewable energy planning, waste reduction, and ecosystem-based adaptation.
